scenario: A film school admits students if they have either elite cinematography skill or elite editing skill. A 10% wildcard also admits applicants with neither trait. Faculty infer a negative relationship between cinematography and editing among the admitted class.

data.description: Admission is based on either trait plus a wildcard.

question: Among admitted students, compute (a) P(cinematography | editing, selected), and (b) P(cinematography | not editing, selected). Is the negative association real or a selection artifact?

ground_truth.explanation: The school's admission rule induces collider bias.

naive_answer: Editing and cinematography seem negatively related in the admitted class, so the talents probably substitute.
naive_trap: Conditioning on admission creates a false negative association.
